source_caption_text:
The beat pause before Key Glock’s entry on this goes too hard 😤🔥

Young Dolph and Key Glock had a chemistry that always made their collaborations hit different, and “No Sense” is a perfect example. Released in 2020 on Dolph’s Rich Slave album, the track brings together their laid-back flows over heavy production from Supah Mario and Cassius Jay.

One of the hardest moments comes right before Key Glock’s verse. Dolph cuts the beat completely, leaving a brief pause before Glock comes in. It’s such a simple touch, but it makes his entrance hit that much harder.

The two go back and forth with their confident deliveries, trading lines about their success and everything they’ve worked for. “No Sense” is a reminder of how naturally Dolph and Glock worked together, and why fans still go back to their music.
